title: N-2 ascends along a finite extension of Noetherian domains
statement: Let $A\subseteq B$ be integral domains such that $B$ is a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Assume $A$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Then $B$ is N-2: for every finite field extension $M$ [def-pc-field-extension] of the fraction field of $B$, the integral closure of $B$ in $M$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $B$-module.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), in the case of a finite extension named there ('quasi-finite extension of domains (for example finite)'); its proof, second paragraph ('Assume $R\subset S$ ... moreover that $S$ is finite over $R$ ... we win by Lemma integral-permanence'), lines 45225-45232

proof.text: *Fraction fields.* Let $K=A_{(0)}$ and $L=B_{(0)}$ be the fraction fields of $A$ and $B$, their localizations at the prime $(0)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Since $A\subseteq B\subseteq L$ and every nonzero $s\in A$ is nonzero in the field $L$, the map $\iota:K\to L$, $a/s\mapsto as^{-1}$, is well defined ($a/s=a'/s'$ means $as'=a's$ in the domain $A$, hence in $L$), a ring homomorphism, and injective since $K$ is a field; on $A$ it is the inclusion $A\subseteq B\subseteq L$. So $L$ is a field extension of $K$ through $\iota$ [def-pc-field-extension], and for any field extension $M$ of $L$ the two $A$-algebra structures on $M$, through $A\subseteq K\xrightarrow{\iota}L\subseteq M$ and through $A\subseteq B\subseteq L\subseteq M$, agree.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, first paragraph, lines 45208-45209: 'Let $L/K$ be the induced extension of fraction fields.'

proof.text: *$E/K$ is finite.* The injective map $A\to B$ gives faithful scalar multiplication. Since $B$ is finite over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], it is integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], hence algebraic. Mathlib's Algebra.IsAlgebraic instance identifies the fraction field $E$ as the localization of $B$ at the images of the nonzero elements of $A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]: every nonzero element of $B$ divides a nonzero element of $A$, by algebraicity. Choose finite module generators using Module.Finite.exists_fin. Their images span $E$ over $K$ by span_eq_top_localization_localization, so Module.finite_def and Submodule.fg_span give FiniteDimensional K E [def-pc-field-extension]. This implements the finite-case fibre argument of the source without the intermediate finite-dimensional-domain-is-a-field lemma.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, first paragraph, lines 45209-45212: 'Note that this is a finite field extension (for example by Lemma isolated-point-fibre (2) applied to the fibre $S\otimes_R K$ ...)', in the finite case

proof.text: *$M/K$ is finite.* Let $M$ be a finite field extension of $L$ [def-pc-field-extension]. By steps 1 and 2, $K\subseteq L\subseteq M$ (through $\iota$) with $L/K$ and $M/L$ finite, so by the tower law [lem-weil-pbc-field-degree-multiplicativity] $M/K$ is finite, with $[M:K]=[M:L][L:K]$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, second paragraph, lines 45226-45228: 'Let $M$ be a finite field extension of the fraction field of $S$. Then $M$ is also a finite field extension of $K$'

proof.text: *The closure of $A$.* For an arbitrary finite field extension $M/E$, construct the $K$-algebra structure by composition and the $A$-algebra structure through $B$, checking that the two towers agree. Step 3 gives Module.Finite K M. The definition IsN2 A K [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] tests fields in the universe of $K$, so use Module.Finite.small K M and Shrink to represent $M$ in that universe. Shrink.algEquiv transports its field and algebra structures, and its scalar-tower identity follows from AlgEquiv.commutes. Apply IsN2 A K to this shrunken finite extension. Its integral closure [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is finite over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Transport this finiteness back along Shrink.algEquiv.mapIntegralClosure.toLinearEquiv using Module.Finite.equiv; thus integralClosure A M is finite over $A$. Shrink is an equivalence construction, not an arbitrary choice of a field from an unproved existence theorem.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, second paragraph, lines 45228-45229: 'and we conclude that the integral closure $T$ of $R$ in $M$ is finite over $R$'

proof.text: *The two closures have the same elements.* Define the $A$-linear map from integralClosure A M to integralClosure B M [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] to be the identity on underlying elements. IsIntegral.tower_top shows that an element integral over $A$ is integral over $B$. Conversely Module.Finite A B gives Algebra.IsIntegral A B [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral], and isIntegral_trans [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive] shows that every element integral over $B$ is integral over $A$. This gives an explicit preimage for every element and proves surjectivity of the linear map, without changing either integral-closure definition.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032I (lemma-quasi-finite-over-Noetherian-japanese, line 45202), proof, second paragraph, lines 45229-45230: 'By Lemma integral-closure-transitive [Tag 0308] we see that $T$ is also the integral closure of $S$ in $M$'

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By Module.Finite.of_surjective applied to the map of step 5, integralClosure B M is finite over $A$. Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite A B then makes it finite over $B$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]: the same finite generators suffice over the larger scalar ring. Since $M/E$ was arbitrary, this proves IsN2 B E [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. As in the source's finite case, the Noetherian hypothesis is unused and retained unchanged.
